title: How do we add thirteen sums of fractions?
description: Thirteen sums of fractions are added with one method. The fractions are written with a common bottom number, the top numbers are added, and each sum is checked against the greatest fraction added.
teaching_notes: One idea: make the fractional units the same, then add the numerators. The method is the same for two fractions, three fractions and tops bigger than bottoms. Watch for students who add the bottom numbers.

video_script.why: A learner adds fractions by the solved examples: find a common bottom number, rewrite every fraction with it, add the top numbers, reduce if possible, and check against the greatest fraction added.
video_script.anchor: thirteen sums of fractions written on the board
video_script.payoff_line: make the units the same, then add the numerators

final_answer.spoken: the sums are thirteen sevenths, thirteen twelfths, three halves, twenty over twenty-one, seventy-seven sixtieths, twenty-two fifteenths twice, forty-nine fortieths, twenty-three fourths, sixty-two over twenty-one, seventy-seven sixtieths, one hundred and ninety-nine over one hundred and five, and eighty-three twelfths

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, with thirteen sums to add.
<bookmark mark='sums'/>We must use {{NAME_2}}'s method for every sum.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How can one method add them all?

beats.on_screen: the grid holds still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: two fractions with the same bottom number being counted together, then two fractions with different bottom numbers and a question mark

marks.unit: two fractions with the same bottom number are counted together
marks.differ: two fractions with different bottom numbers sit side by side with a question mark

narration: <bookmark mark='unit'/>Fractions can be added only when they have the same fractional unit.
<bookmark mark='differ'/>If the bottom numbers differ, we first make them the same.

beats.on_screen: Given: 13 sums; some have two fractions and some have three

marks.given: the line about the thirteen sums is written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, there are thirteen sums, and some have two fractions while others have three.
<bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find every sum.

marks.same: 2/7, 5/7 and 6/7 are written with the bottom number 7 circled

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step one, two sevenths, five sevenths and six sevenths already share a bottom number.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Add the top numbers: two plus five plus six is thirteen, so the sum is thirteen sevenths.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: no common factor, so multiply the bottom numbers: 3/4 + 1/3 = 9/12 + 4/12 = 13/12; 2/3 + 2/7 = 14/21 + 6/21 = 20/21

marks.rule: the words multiply the bottom numbers are written

beats.colours: the common bottom number = accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, when the bottom numbers share no factor, multiply them to get the common bottom number.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Three fourths and one third use twelve, giving nine twelfths plus four twelfths. That is thirteen twelfths.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Two thirds and two sevenths use twenty-one, giving fourteen over twenty-one plus six over twenty-one. That is twenty over twenty-one.

marks.order: 4/5 + 2/3 is written below with the same result 22/15

beats.colours: the common bottom number = accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='swap'/>Step three, two thirds and four fifths use fifteen, giving ten fifteenths plus twelve fifteenths. That is twenty-two fifteenths.
<bookmark mark='order'/>Four fifths and two thirds give the same sum, because the order of adding does not matter.
<bookmark mark='third'/>Three fifths and five eighths use forty, giving twenty-four fortieths plus twenty-five fortieths. That is forty-nine fortieths.

marks.sum: 4/6 + 5/6 = 9/6 and the top and bottom are divided by 3 to give 3/2

beats.colours: the common bottom number = accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='six'/>Step four, three goes into six, so two thirds and five sixths use six. Two thirds becomes four sixths.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Four sixths plus five sixths is nine sixths. Divide the top and the bottom by three, and we get three halves.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>Nine halves and five fourths use four, giving eighteen fourths plus five fourths. That is twenty-three fourths.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>Eight thirds and two sevenths use twenty-one, giving fifty-six over twenty-one plus six over twenty-one. That is sixty-two over twenty-one.

marks.three: the words one common bottom number for all three are written

beats.colours: the common bottom number = accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step five, with three fractions we find one common bottom number for all of them.
<bookmark mark='sixty'/>Three fourths, one third and one fifth use sixty, so the tops become forty-five, twenty and twelve. Their sum is seventy-seven sixtieths.
<bookmark mark='hundred'/>Two thirds, four fifths and three sevenths use one hundred and five. The tops become seventy, eighty-four and forty-five.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Their sum is one hundred and ninety-nine over one hundred and five.
<bookmark mark='twelve'/>Nine halves, five fourths and seven sixths use twelve. The tops become fifty-four, fifteen and fourteen, and their sum is eighty-three twelfths.

beats.on_screen: Check: each sum is greater than the greatest fraction added; 83/12 > 54/12; 3/2 > 5/6

marks.check: the words sum greater than the greatest fraction are written

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step six, check each sum. It must be greater than the greatest fraction we added.
<bookmark mark='ex'/>Nine halves is fifty-four twelfths, and eighty-three twelfths is greater.
<bookmark mark='ex2'/>Two thirds and five sixths give three halves, which is greater than five sixths.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The first four sums are thirteen sevenths, thirteen twelfths, three halves and twenty over twenty-one.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>Next come seventy-seven sixtieths, twenty-two fifteenths twice, forty-nine fortieths and twenty-three fourths.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The last four are sixty-two over twenty-one and seventy-seven sixtieths. Then come one hundred and ninety-nine over one hundred and five, and eighty-three twelfths.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>In every sum, make the units the same, then add the numerators.
